newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares ease, Hermis maintains fall.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares ease, Hermis maintains fall.

text.p: Lithuanian shares eased in light trade on Friday and one of the leading commercial banks, Hermis Bank, continued to suffer, dealers said.
Overall central market volume was just over 600,000 litas and the group A index dropped by 5.54 points to 2,468.75.
"The market was very quiet today, but things should pick up after all of the 1996 results are clear," Arvydas Jacekevicius of Suprema brokerage house told Reuters.
Hermis Bank continued to lose ground, falling to 185.00 litas from 189.90 litas in trade of 42,550 litas.
Dealers say the market anticipates that 1996 net profit may fall short of the 25 million litas previously expected.
"Hermis Bank paid out dividends last year based on the 3.6 million litas profit figure which showed on the results based on Lithuanian accounting procedures," one dealer told Reuters.

"But its results based on international accounting standards in 1995 showed a loss and so this year it may have to make up the difference. This will reduce its profit, but the profit should still be healthy," the dealer added.
Dealers were also optimistic after the announcement today that J.P. Morgan is to lead a $200 million eurobond.
"The Eurobond issue that was announced today should help bring more attention to the Lithuanian market," he added.
Birzai Dairy's shares remained in relative demand in turnover of 100,400 litas at the unchanged price of 10.00 litas.
Kaunas Fabrics was one of the few gainers, advancing to 1.08 litas from 1.03 litas in trade of 52,610 litas.
The Lithuania Sea Shipping Company turned over 186,000 litas at the unchanged price of 6.85 litas.
Block trades worth 21,700 litas were also made and the secondary T-bill market turned over less than 10,000 litas.
